dimensions.name: Reference mining & contract inference

evidence.note: Systematically mapped the Vite/plugin-rsc API surface early: read plugin-rsc package, .d.ts types, RscPluginOptions, react runtime helper types, README (multiple parts incl. server actions), e2e helpers, and starter examples before writing any code.

Read plugin-rsc core plugin internals (configureServer, serverHandler), entry points, build/environment/jsx config defaults, and html-stream/ssr helpers — grounding the plugin lifecycle understanding in actual source.

Enumerated the exact next/* import specifiers and the named imports per next module used by fixtures — direct contract inference defining what the fixtures require rather than guessing full Next.js API.

Read the specific fixture files for each subsystem (headers/route/action, after/connection, cache, dynamic/og/script) immediately before authoring each shim, tying every shim to an observed usage/contract.

Sustained late-stage re-consultation of upstream source to resolve edge-case semantics as they surfaced: action wire protocol in browser.js, browser.d.ts exports, README browser-hydration pattern, plugin-rsc type defs — preventing rework on RSC/action/hydration behavior.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's action pattern is dense, targeted reference mining that begins with a systematic mapping of the Vite plugin-rsc API surface and README, then infers exact next/* contracts by enumerating fixture imports (steps 176/179), and grounds every shim in the corresponding fixture read immediately before writing it. Crucially the research is sustained throughout the build — it repeatedly re-consults upstream dist/README/type-defs to resolve ambiguous edge-case semantics (action serialization wire protocol, RSC boundaries, browser hydration) as they surface late in the trajectory (steps 657, 739-744), and distinguishes fixture-required behavior from full Next.js. This matches the level-8 anchor fully and reaches into level-10 territory on sustained cross-referencing; I withhold a 10 only because the summarized trajectory doesn't surface explicit written notes of the semantics, landing it at 9.

dimensions.name: Subsystem decomposition & sequencing

evidence.note: Creates 6 tasks partitioning the framework into subsystems in a dependency-aware order: CLI+main plugin (resolution foundation) → next/* shims → app-router/RSC/SSR → pages routing + getStaticProps/Paths → middleware/config/ISR → build+run test suite. Sensible ordering (resolution/plugin before routing before SSR/SSG) but subsystem-grouped feature buckets, not an early end-to-end slice.
TaskUpdate status toggles (in_progress/completed) show the agent tracked milestone boundaries as it worked through the planned subsystems.

First actual integration run (pack tarball, start dev server, fetch page) happens only at the very end after all subsystems were built; no thin vertical slice validated early and no test-gated milestone progression — falls short of the level-8 'minimal end-to-end path first' anchor.

Implementation follows the task order (package.json/cli/plugin → shims → app-router runtime → pages runtime → middleware) confirming the sequence was executed, but each milestone was not proven against fixtures/tests before moving on.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent produced a real subsystem decomposition (steps 90-95) with a defensible dependency order — plugin/resolution foundation before routing before SSR/SSG before middleware and build/test — and tracked milestones via TaskUpdate, which clearly exceeds the flat requirement-mirroring of level 3. But it never established an early thin vertical slice: the first end-to-end dev-server run comes only at the very end (steps 800+), and milestones were feature buckets not tied to concrete test subsets that gate progress, so it does not reach the level-8 pattern of proving a minimal path before layering features. This places it squarely at level 5.

dimensions.name: Test-driven verification design

evidence.note: Planned a task to run npm run build and the Playwright suite via run_tests.sh and fix failures until pass — intent to use the suite as an oracle, but this is planning not execution.
Read run_tests.sh / run_tests.py and inspected the test harness to understand how verification would work, though without yet running it.
Smoke-checked the plugin import — a fast targeted probe beyond 'it compiles'.
Packed the tarball, prepared the pages-basic fixture, started a dev server, and curled the home page — manually standing up a fixture to observe SSR/dev behavior.
Edited navigation-client.js in response to the observed fetch output, then repacked/reinstalled — using a fixture observation to guide a concrete fix (dev path).
The bulk of the trajectory is reading and writing code with no execution or verification at all; verification only emerges near the end.

dimensions.reasoning: For most of the horizon the agent verified nothing, writing large amounts of code before running anything (below the 3 anchor for that span), but near the end it does real targeted probing: smoke-testing the import, standing up the pages fixture on a dev server, curling it, and using the observed output to guide a fix — matching the level-5 anchor of running individual fixtures for the subsystem in progress and using observations to drive fixes, verifying the dev path. It falls short of level 8 because no full-suite regression gating, no production build/start verification, and no designed multi-subsystem verification loop are observed within the (apparently truncated) trajectory.

dimensions.name: Progress & pass-rate tracking across subsystems

evidence.note: Created a structured task list decomposing the framework into subsystems, including a final 'run npm run build, run playwright suite, fix failures until all pass' task — establishing a done-vs-pending frame at the subsystem level.
TaskUpdate calls mark subsystems in_progress/completed, maintaining a coarse subsystem-level progress picture — but status is self-declared, not tied to any test-pass evidence.
Repeatedly read run_tests.sh / run_tests.py but the trajectory contains no step actually executing the full suite to obtain pass/fail counts; pass-rate is never measured or tracked.

Only late-stage verification is a single manual smoke test (dev server + curl) that surfaces a nav bug and a fix; reactive, one-off, and the run ends at 'repack/reinstall' without ever running the Playwright suite.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintained a subsystem-level done-vs-pending view via a task tracker, which lifts it above the 'vague recollection' of anchor 3, but it never ran the test suite to obtain pass counts and never re-checked changes against tests to catch regressions — the core of anchor 5. With no test-evidence-based pass-rate model, no regression detection, and only a single late reactive smoke test, its behavior sits between anchors 3 and 5, landing at 4.

dimensions.name: Design revision under divergence

evidence.note: After ~7 incremental Edits to pages-ssr.jsx failed to settle it, the agent abandons patching and does a full Write/rewrite (725), then adds pages-handler.jsx (728) and re-integrates entry.ssr.jsx (730) — a subsystem rework absorbing cost rather than continuing to patch.

Creates unified-request-context.js consolidating the earlier separate request-context.js (191) across routers — a genuine architectural consolidation of a cross-cutting concern, suggesting recognition the split design was problematic.
app-router-match.js rewritten three times and app-render.jsx twice, but during initial construction — iterative refinement rather than clearly divergence-triggered foundational revision.

First runtime smoke test (dev server) reveals an issue; the agent responds with local navigation-client.js edits — a local fix. The trajectory ends here, before any full test-suite-driven divergence phase.

dimensions.reasoning: The visible trajectory (which cuts off during the first smoke test, before the test-failure debugging phase) shows the agent willing to rework whole subsystems rather than only patch — notably the clean pages-ssr rewrite after failed incremental edits and the request-context consolidation into a unified module — behavior above the pure local-patching of anchor 3. However, most rework is construction-time iteration, the one captured divergence (802-811) is met with a local fix, and there is no visible evidence of foundational pivots deliberately triggered by accumulating failures with re-verification of dependents (anchor 8). This places the observed behavior between anchors 3 and 5, at 4; confidence is low because the log lacks observation/prose content and is truncated before the divergence-heavy phase.

dimensions.name: Resisting overfit to the visible suite

evidence.note: Enumerated all next/* import specifiers and named imports per module, building to the full API surface rather than only the symbols individual tests exercise — a generalization-oriented move.

Implemented a distinct semantic shim for each next/* module (navigation, headers, server, cache, dynamic, image, form, router, head, document, og, font) rather than hard-coding fixture outputs; behavior-level implementation.
Repeatedly read e2e specs alongside fixtures and reference source/types, treating tests as a sample of behavior to implement generally rather than targets to satisfy literally.
Repeatedly consulted plugin-rsc type defs and README and browser hydration contract to implement real semantics; no observed fixture-specific shortcuts or hard-coded values.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently implemented actual per-subsystem/per-module semantics inferred from shim type contracts, upstream source, and the full import surface (steps 176-251), with no observed hard-coding or fixture-specific special-casing, and it read specs as a sample rather than the target — matching the level-5 anchor. However, the (summary-form) trajectory shows no explicit reasoning about the visible-vs-hidden test gap and no stress-testing of behaviors beyond what the visible tests exercise, which the level-8/10 anchors require, so it falls at 5 rather than higher.

rubric.task_read: This is a maximally long-horizon, high-complexity build: reimplement the core of Next.js (CLI, Pages + App routers, SSR, SSG, `use cache`, server actions, middleware, `after()`, client hooks, and a Vite plugin that shims `next/*`) as a single `vinext` package on Vite's plugin API, with no internet and only vendored source to learn from. Difficulty comes from the sheer surface area, tightly-coupled subsystems, contracts that must be reverse-engineered from vendored Next.js/Vite source and fixture `next-shims.d.ts`, and a moving target (335 visible → 373 hidden tests). A skilled practitioner would invest heavily and continuously in every meta-work faculty; ceremony risk is low, thrash-and-lose-the-plot risk is very high.

dimensions.name: Reference mining & contract inference
dimensions.description: Studying vendored Vite/Next.js source and fixture type shims to understand the Vite plugin API and the exact `next/*` contracts before and while implementing, rather than guessing framework semantics.
dimensions.why_it_matters: There is no internet; correct behavior lives entirely in the vendored source and the fixtures' `next-shims.d.ts`. Guessing Next.js semantics or the Vite plugin lifecycle guarantees rework across a huge surface.

anchors.0: Starts coding shims/routing from memory of Next.js without opening any reference or fixture file.
anchors.3: Skims one or two reference files or a fixture shim, then proceeds mostly on assumption; contracts are inferred loosely.
anchors.5: Reads the relevant Vite plugin API surface and the fixture `next-shims.d.ts` for the subsystem currently being built; grounds each `next/*` shim in an actual type signature.
anchors.8: Systematically maps the vendored Next.js source and Vite plugin hooks to the required subsystems, extracts precise contracts from every fixture shim, and re-consults source when behavior is ambiguous rather than guessing; notes non-obvious semantics (e.g. RSC boundaries, cache keys, action serialization).
anchors.10: Sustained, targeted research throughout the build: continuously cross-references upstream source to resolve edge-case semantics as they surface, distinguishes what the fixtures actually require from full Next.js behavior, and builds an accurate mental/written model of how routing, RSC, and module resolution interlock — visibly preventing whole classes of rework.

dimensions.name: Subsystem decomposition & sequencing
dimensions.description: Breaking the framework into ordered, independently-verifiable subsystems (module shim/resolution, dev server, routing, SSR, SSG, caching, actions, CLI/build) with a dependency-aware sequence and done-criteria per milestone.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The subsystems are tightly coupled and one package must ship all of them; without dependency-aware sequencing and explicit milestones the agent will build in an order that forces constant backtracking and never reaches a testable state.

anchors.0: Treats the whole thing as one undifferentiated coding push; no ordering or sub-goals.
anchors.3: A flat, generic list mirroring the requirement bullets, with no dependency ordering or done-criteria.
anchors.5: Identifies the major subsystems and picks a sensible order (e.g. resolution/plugin before routing before SSR/SSG), with a rough notion of when each is 'done'.
anchors.8: Dependency-aware milestone plan that sequences a minimal end-to-end path (one route rendering under dev) before layering features, each milestone tied to concrete fixtures/tests that prove it, and revisited as the build reveals coupling.
anchors.10: A living decomposition that establishes a thin vertical slice early, orders remaining subsystems to maximize how soon tests can gate progress, explicitly manages interfaces between subsystems so they compose, and re-plans milestone boundaries as integration realities emerge — never losing the through-line across the long horizon.

dimensions.name: Test-driven verification design
dimensions.description: Deliberately using and extending the Playwright suite and fixture apps as checks — running targeted subsets per subsystem, building smaller probes, and verifying behavior beyond just 'it compiles'.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The 335-test suite is the ground truth, but it is slow and coarse; verifying each subsystem needs faster, targeted checks and running the right fixtures, or the agent flies blind between rare full-suite runs.

anchors.0: Never runs the test suite or the fixture apps; assumes correctness from the code alone.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally as a pass/fail oracle with no targeted or intermediate verification.
anchors.5: Runs relevant test subsets / individual fixtures for the subsystem in progress and uses failures to guide fixes; verifies dev and build paths work.
anchors.8: Designs a verification loop: fast targeted checks per subsystem, standing up fixtures manually to observe SSR/SSG/action behavior, and using the suite as a regression gate rather than a debugger; confirms both `dev` and the production `build`/`start` paths.
anchors.10: Builds a deliberate, layered verification strategy — minimal reproductions for hard subsystems (RSC, caching, actions), interprets test failures by root cause rather than symptom, and actively probes behaviors the visible suite may under-cover, treating passing tests as necessary-not-sufficient evidence of a faithful reimplementation.

dimensions.name: Progress & pass-rate tracking across subsystems
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate, current picture of which subsystems/tests pass vs. remain, and detecting circular debugging or regressions across a very large surface.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With hundreds of tests and many interdependent subsystems over a long horizon, it is easy to fix one area while regressing another, or to loop on the same failure; an accurate done-vs-remaining picture is what sustains forward motion.

anchors.0: No tracking of what passes or what is left; works reactively with no sense of overall state.
anchors.3: Vague recollection of progress; notices only whatever failure is in front of it.
anchors.5: Tracks pass counts / which subsystems are done and which are pending, and re-checks after changes to catch obvious regressions.
anchors.8: Maintains a structured, updated view of pass-rate by area, watches for regressions when touching shared code, and recognizes when it is looping on one failure and steps back rather than retrying blindly.
anchors.10: Continuously reconciles a precise model of done-vs-remaining against real test evidence across the whole surface, catches subtle cross-subsystem regressions early, quantifies progress toward the full suite, and reallocates effort to the highest-leverage remaining failures rather than drifting.

dimensions.name: Design revision under divergence
dimensions.description: Revising the architecture or approach (module resolution scheme, rendering pipeline, cache/action wiring) when reality — failing tests or discovered semantics — contradicts the initial design, rather than patching around a flawed foundation.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Early architectural choices (how `next/*` is intercepted, how RSC/SSR is wired into Vite) will be partly wrong; the agent must be willing to refactor the foundation instead of piling hacks that make later subsystems impossible.

anchors.0: Barrels ahead on the original approach even as failures accumulate; only adds patches.
anchors.3: Makes local fixes when something breaks but never revisits an underlying design decision even when it is clearly the cause.
anchors.5: Recognizes when an approach is wrong and reworks that subsystem, absorbing the cost rather than hacking around it.
anchors.8: Detects when a foundational choice (resolution, render pipeline) is blocking multiple subsystems and refactors it deliberately, updating the plan and re-verifying dependents afterward.
anchors.10: Treats falsified assumptions as signals to rethink the design cleanly, weighs refactor-vs-workaround explicitly, executes foundational pivots without losing already-passing behavior, and emerges with a more coherent architecture — demonstrating sustained self-correction across the horizon.

dimensions.name: Resisting overfit to the visible suite
dimensions.description: Implementing faithful, general framework behavior rather than special-casing the 335 visible tests, given explicit notice that 373 hidden tests over the same behavior will judge the work.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec openly states the final grade uses a larger hidden suite covering the same behaviors; an agent that hard-codes to visible fixtures will pass locally and fail the real metric, so recognizing and countering this gap is a distinct, decisive meta-work demand.

anchors.0: Hard-codes outputs or narrowly special-cases the visible fixtures/tests to turn them green.
anchors.3: Mostly general but reaches for a fixture-specific shortcut when a behavior is hard, without noting the risk.
anchors.5: Implements the actual semantics for each behavior rather than test-specific hacks, aware the suite is a sample not the target.
anchors.8: Explicitly reasons about the visible-vs-hidden gap, generalizes each subsystem to the real Next.js contract from the reference, and avoids overfitting even under schedule pressure.
anchors.10: Systematically implements to the general contract inferred from upstream source and shim types, stress-tests behaviors beyond what the visible tests exercise to expose overfit, and can articulate why the implementation should hold on unseen cases of the same behavior.
